claims.text: Anti-inflam drugs may resolve the transient constriction seen in 10–20% of cases w.in a few months.
claims.quote: medical therapy (generally based on anti-inflammatory drugs) may solve the transient constriction occurring in 10–20% of cases within a few months

claims.text: ↑CRP and imaging evidence of pericardial inflam may help identify potentially reversible cases.
claims.quote: The detection of elevated CRP and imaging evidence of pericardial inflammation by contrast enhancement on CT and/or CMR may be helpful to identify patients with potentially reversible forms of constriction

claims.text: Newly diagnosed constrictive pericarditis, hemodynamically stable, ⍉chronic constriction: may get a 3-month trial of anti-inflammatories rather than pericardiectomy.
claims.quote: Patients with newly diagnosed constrictive pericarditis who are hemodynamically stable and without evidence of chronic constriction may be given a 3-month trial of anti-inflammatory medications, rather than pericardiectomy
